skeptic

SKEP-tik -- from Greek skeptikos, 'thoughtful, reflective,' from skeptesthai ('to look, consider'), related to the root behind '-scope' words like telescope. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Skeptic is one who doubts accepted opinions.

As a lifelong skeptic, she refused to accept the miracle cure's claims without seeing the clinical trial data herself.

Example

A newspaper reports a sensational headline about a diet that melts pounds overnight, and one skeptic among the readers, instead of sharing it, immediately searches for the original study.

That habit of doubting a claim until real evidence backs it up, rather than accepting it just because it sounds convincing, is exactly what makes someone a skeptic.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

cynic: A cynic assumes the worst about people, suspecting that every motive hides selfishness or an angle. A skeptic doubts claims rather than people: show a skeptic solid evidence and the doubt gives way, while the cynic goes on distrusting whoever produced it.

disbeliever: A disbeliever has already made up their mind that something is false and simply refuses to accept it. A skeptic has not decided at all: a skeptic withholds judgment, asks for the evidence, and remains genuinely willing to be convinced either way.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

believer: a person who accepts something as true

convert: a person who has fully accepted a new belief

Where it sits · how wide the distrust reaches — doubter → skeptic → denier

doubter vs. skeptic: Doubter is the plainer, more neutral word -- a doubter simply questions a specific claim, while skeptic often implies a more systematic habit of demanding evidence before believing anything.

denier vs. skeptic: A denier goes further than a skeptic -- a skeptic withholds belief until the evidence arrives, while a denier keeps rejecting a claim even after solid evidence has piled up.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — skept-/skop-

root — skept-/skop-: to look, consider, examine (Greek (skeptesthai/skopein))

Put it together

Put it together: Skeptic comes from Greek skeptikos, 'thoughtful, reflective,' from skeptesthai, 'to look or consider' -- a root closely related to the Greek skopein ('to look at, examine') that also gives English words ending in '-scope,' since a skeptic 'looks closely' at a claim before accepting it.

Use the root in a new word: telescope

Use the root in a new word: telescope: The astronomy club unveiled a new telescope powerful enough to photograph distant nebulae in stunning detail.

Word Building

Word Choice

Skeptic describes a person's habit of mind -- someone who withholds belief until convinced by solid evidence. The related adjective is 'skeptical,' as in 'she remained skeptical of the salesman's promises.'
